Subject: Re: Post-call recap — next steps and tests

Thanks for the call earlier, Tessa — good overview. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Our top priority is predictable 99th percentile latency for short queries (<= 128 tokens) across off-peak and peak windows.
- Cost-per-1k-tokens is important but secondary to latency for now.
- Security: SOC 2 attestation and VPC options are mandatory; we also need an audit log sample.

We reviewed the candidate vendors and want to focus tests on three capabilities: latency SLOs under concurrency, KV cache effectiveness for chat history, and failure/fallback behavior during regional failover.

Can you share the prioritization matrix you mentioned and a proposed POA for tests next week? Also forwarding to procurement for visibility.

Best,
Emma
Director, Platform Engineering
Medisys Health

Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis: prioritization matrix, decision weights & next tests

Emma — thanks for the clear priorities and for looping procurement in. Per our discussion, attached is the prioritization matrix (weights column filled with our recommended starting point) and a short POA for the proposed validation tests. High-level summary and asks below.

Summary of customer priorities (confirmed):
1) 99th pct latency guarantees for short queries (<=128 tokens) under concurrency up to 250qps per pod.
2) Deterministic failover behavior with automatic routing to warm model variant (no data loss).
3) KV cache persistence across short chat sessions (10–50 messages) to reduce per-token compute.
4) SOC 2 + VPC + audit logs sample required.

What we propose (next week validation windows):
- Baseline latency sweep (single-cluster, 1–250 concurrent users) against their typical prompt set; target: document 99th pct and P95 across short/long queries. (Owner: David)
- KV cache smoke tests using a 20-message chat replay (compare end-to-end token cost and latency with/without KV cache). (Owner: Marissa)
- Regional failover drill: simulate node and AZ loss and observe routing and SLA behavior (Owner: Tessa).
- Security artifacts: attach SOC 2 summary and a 72-hour sample of audit logs to the shared Drive link. (Owner: Tessa)

Deliverables and dates:
- POA and test schedule (this doc) — shared now.
- Test data + scripts — 2026-12-15.
- Test run and recordings — 2026-12-16 to 2026-12-17.
- Results and prioritized action list — by 2026-12-18 EOD.

Immediate asks for Medisys: please confirm the concurrency target (we used 250qps/pod as discussed) and provide a redacted sample of their prompt traffic (5–10 examples) for realistic latencies. Also confirm if procurement needs an estimated cost delta for a dedicated pool vs hosted.

Attachments: medisys-priority-matrix.xlsx; poa-test-plan.md

Thanks — I’ll kick off the runbook once we get the confirmations.

—Tessa
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
